sample_unit: chatbot-generated texts on appendicitis (one per chatbot)

links.outcome: Readability (FKGL, FRE) of chatbot-generated appendicitis information versus public reading level
links.effect: FKGL and FRE were 14.6/23.8 (ChatGPT-3.5), 11.9/33.9 (ChatGPT-4), 8.6/52.8 (Bard), 11.0/36.6 (Claude-2), indicating college-level difficulty.
links.quote: Regarding readability, FKGL and FRE scores of ChatGPT-3.5, ChatGPT-4, Bard, and Claude-2 were 14.6 and 23.8, 11.9 and 33.9, 8.6 and 52.8, 11.0 and 36.6, respectively, indicating difficulty readability at a college reading skill level.

links.outcome: Presence and verifiability of sources cited in chatbot outputs
links.effect: Bard was the only platform listing verifiable sources; Claude-2 provided fabricated sources; most fabricated sources or gave none.
links.quote: Bard was the only AI platform that listed verifiable sources, while Claude-2 provided fabricated sources.

links.outcome: Reading level of patient-directed generative AI content
links.effect: Overall readability far exceeded recommended levels for the public; FKGL ranged 8.6 to 14.6.
links.quote: Additionally, overall readability far exceeded recommended levels for the public.

links.outcome: Whether chatbot responses advised consulting a physician for symptoms
links.effect: All chatbots except Claude-2 advised readers to consult a physician if experiencing symptoms.
links.quote: All chatbots except for Claude-2 advised readers to consult a physician if experiencing symptoms.

screen.reason: Evaluates the quality, readability, and source verification of medical information about appendicitis generated by four commercial LLMs without testing a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
